quotes.text: Autonomy is just the ability to act without someone stopping you, but sovereignty is something much more valuable. It is predictability.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines tenant sovereignty crisply by contrasting it with autonomy.

quotes.text: If your system design allows standing global admin access to exist, then your architecture is broken. The people aren't the problem. The design is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes over-privileged admins as an architecture failure, not a training failure.

quotes.text: Configuration drift is an architectural failure. If your security baseline is configured once and then left to drift over time, you no longer have a baseline. You have a memory and in complex systems, memory always fails.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable argument for configuration as code over one-time baselines.

quotes.text: Boundary control is not about restricting collaboration, but rather about making every data flow explicit and auditable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the purpose of tenant boundaries in one sentence.

quotes.text: If you have a co-pilot instance designed to summarize emails it should have read access to the inbox but no permission to delete or send messages.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete, practical illustration of least-privilege scoping for agents.

takeaways: Treat the Microsoft 365 tenant as a deterministic system that is explicitly designed, where every policy has intent, every permission a boundary and every change is reconcilable.

Build the seven layers in sequence, starting with time-bound identity through PIM and conditional access, then boundaries, configuration as code, lifecycle, agent governance, operations and continuous assessment.
Make sovereignty measurable with a scorecard reviewed quarterly by leadership, so governance depends on architectural enforcement rather than people remembering to do the right thing.
hook: Most Microsoft 365 tenants work on the surface while policies drift, permissions sprawl and AI agents inherit every forgotten exception. This episode gives architects, security and IT leaders a seven-layer framework and phased roadmap to move from accidental configuration to an intentionally controlled, measurable sovereign tenant.
